title: The sync gate passes a host's known-red tests recorded at the integration main, and names each in its report
goal: tests.py --changed under the sync gate reads a list of test ids known to fail on this platform at the integration main (_tools/known_red.csv: platform, test id, the bug item filed for it); a run whose only failures are listed ids passes, the gate prints each known-red id it met and each listed id that now passes (to take out), and the test.run and sync.gate ops rows count them (known_red, known_fixed), so the logs, not a red gate, carry them; an unlisted failure still fails the gate; the list is written by a command that runs the listed tests at origin/main, so an id that passes there is refused; planted cases: a listed failure passes the gate and is named, an unlisted one fails it, a listed id that passes is reported, a hand-added id that passes at origin/main is refused

gates.question: May the sync gate pass on test failures recorded as known on a platform, and where does that list live? committed = _tools/known_red.csv in the repository, one row per test id with its platform and bug item, written only by the record command at origin/main and reviewed in commits like code; host-local = a list kept per clone under _cache/ (never committed), written by the same command, so each host decides alone; none = no baseline: the gate stays red on the Windows host until its pre-existing failures are fixed

notes: Premise (run on the Windows host before a sprint commits it, the session ST-pg5jyebo's trigger waits for): python3 _tools/tests.py at origin/main exits 1 with the host's pre-existing failures (35, the operator's count), so every sync gate whose selection holds one of them is red there whatever the change, and an all gate (conftest.py, tests.py, testmap.py, pyproject.toml) always is. On macOS the list stays empty: 28 of the 30 whole-suite tests.py runs in the committed ops rows (2026-10-02 to 10-05) are green and the 2 red ones (5 and 1 failures) were green again at the next run. The open Windows bugs (BG-2luo4b26, BG-co3nthy4, BG-ctwgv2lk, BG-hway4bjs, BG-kc7uzged, BG-lt3zjywp, BG-qiib5dow, BG-sivjh67q) are candidate bug items for the rows; a failure no open bug names gets one filed when the list is recorded. Data limit: the committed sidecars hold no row known to come from the Windows host.
